brief: Developments continue with the Borgarlínan project, while the real estate market remains active with several high-value and celebrity property transactions reported. In policy news, a human rights office has been closed and information officers laid off, with further public sector cuts also announced. Concerns are being raised regarding pension security amidst these changes. On a positive note, a missing girl has been safely located.

items.title: Mikil­vægur á­fangi fyrir eldri öku­menn
items.summary: The Icelandic parliament (Alþingi) unanimously approved a bill to change the validity period of driver's licenses for older drivers. This legislative change is described as a significant milestone in the rights of older people.

items.title: Aldrei fleiri Ljón á Ís­landi
items.summary: The article announces a record number of "Lions" in Iceland, referring to the Cannes Lions advertising awards. The chairman of the Association of Icelandic Advertising Agencies expresses pleasure, indicating a significant achievement or participation by Icelandic agencies in this international creative festival.

items.title: Upp­lýsinga­full­trúum sagt upp og mann­réttinda­skrif­stofa lögð niður
items.summary: The Reykjavík City Council has approved the closure of its communications and events department and the city's human rights office. This decision is expected to result in approximately twenty layoffs. A press release regarding these changes is anticipated later today.

items.title: Líf­eyririnn okkar má ekki týnast
items.summary: The article discusses a lecture on the Icelandic public employee pension system, specifically focusing on changes made in 2016 and 2017. It references an article by Professor Gylfi Magnússon from the University of Iceland.
items.spin_note: The headline uses an alarmist tone ("must not be lost") while the body describes attending a lecture about past changes to the pension system, not an immediate threat.

items.title: Súkku­laði hækkað um tæpan þriðjung á tveimur árum
items.summary: A new price survey by ASÍ reveals that the cost of popular chocolate and confectionery products has risen by nearly 33% on average over the past two years. This increase was observed between June 2024 and June 2026.

items.title: Hvaða börn koma fyrst?
items.summary: The article introduces an op-ed by Inga Sæland, the Minister of Education and Children's Affairs. In her piece, titled "Children first, then the system," she announces ambitious new measures. The author of this article notes that many of these proposed actions are positive.
items.spin_note: The headline asks a critical question about which children are prioritized, but the body simply states the minister's proposals are ambitious and largely good, without addressing the headline's implied concern or providing details.

items.title: Kol­finna Niku­lás og Sturla Atlas halda á ný mið
items.summary: The artist couple Kolfinna Nikulásdóttir and Sturla Atlas have put their 84 square meter apartment on Mýrargata up for sale. They are asking for 89.9 million Icelandic krónur for the property.

items.title: Borgarlínan og Línuborg Soria
items.summary: The article discusses Borgarlínan, a public transportation infrastructure project in the capital area. It notes that the project is often framed as a technical endeavor involving new buses, dedicated lanes, and improved public transport. The title also references Soria's Linear City, suggesting a broader urban planning context.

items.title: „Erfiður dagur í ráð­húsinu í dag“
items.summary: The article reports on criticism from the minority in Reykjavík City Council regarding recently announced cuts to the city system. Specific concerns include the closure of the human rights office and the rushed implementation of efficiency measures.

items.title: Boðar frekari niður­skurð
items.summary: The Mayor of Reykjavík, Hildur Björnsdóttir, has announced further budget cuts for the city, following recent reports of mass layoffs. City department heads are now tasked with reviewing their operations to identify areas for these additional reductions.

items.title: Stúlkan er fundin
items.summary: A 17-year-old girl, who had been reported missing by the police twice this week, has been located. The article provides a brief update on her status.

items.title: Gjaldfrjáls Strætó Reykjavíkurbarna kominn og farinn
items.summary: Reykjavík City Council has reversed a recent decision to make bus travel free for all primary school children, just two months after it took effect. The new majority council cited a lack of proper funding and budgeting by the previous administration as the reason for the reversal. Opposition parties expressed disappointment, arguing the policy would have benefited families and encouraged public transport use.

items.title: Nýtt námsefni óaðgengilegra en gömlu bækurnar
items.summary: The article highlights a critical lack of funding for new Icelandic educational materials, forcing them into digital-only formats. Experts warn that this underfunding, which has not increased since 1996 despite significant inflation, threatens the future of the Icelandic language and places an undue burden on teachers.

items.title: Hús sem kemur stórkostlega á óvart í Mosfellsdal
items.summary: This article showcases a 454 sqm property in Mosfellsdal, featuring a 231 sqm main house, an 85 sqm guest house, and a 137 sqm garage/storage. Built between 2018-2026, the modern home boasts an open-plan living area, a master suite with garden access, and three children's rooms with lofts. The property is surrounded by lush greenery, offering privacy and views from a large patio with a hot tub.

items.title: Arnmundur og Ellen selja Vesturbæjarperlu
items.summary: Actors Arnmundur Ernst Backman and Ellen Margrét Bæhrenz are selling their 99-square-meter apartment in Vesturbær, Reykjavík, for 88.9 million ISK. The article describes the apartment's interior, noting its beautiful floating floors, light wood, white fixtures, and a calm atmosphere created by plants and light tones. It also briefly mentions their acting careers.

items.title: Edie Brito selur hönnunaríbúð í Grafarvogi
items.summary: Popular personal trainer Edie Brito is selling her extensively renovated, architect-designed apartment in Grafarvogur. The three-room, 103 sqm property features modern solutions, high-quality materials, and a cohesive design by Brazilian architect Julliana Wagner, including a bright kitchen, open living spaces, and a luxurious bathroom.

items.title: Endurhanna gamalt íslenskt hillukerfi
items.summary: The Icelandic design company Fólk Reykjavík is re-releasing a classic 1972 Icelandic shelving system by Gunnar Magnússon, now called GUNNAR REMIXED. This new version utilizes recycled materials such as rice husk and FSC-certified oak, blending Icelandic design heritage with sustainable innovation. The project, which includes a collaboration with Danish designer Martin Kechayas, is being presented at 3daysofdesign in Copenhagen.

items.title: Gróðurhús og sána í einbýli á Arnarnesinu
items.summary: This article describes a large, renovated detached house for sale in Arnarnes, Garðabær. It highlights unique features like a greenhouse, sauna, and interior design by Rut Káradóttir, along with two additional apartments.

items.title: Raðhús í Reykjavík á undir 100 milljónir
items.summary: This article highlights the increasing rarity of townhouses in Reykjavík due to urban densification. It then presents a curated list of several townhouses currently available for sale in Reykjavík, all priced under 100 million ISK, detailing their locations, sizes, conditions, and asking prices.

items.title: Þrjú fullkomin barnaherbergi í Breiðholtinu
items.summary: The article describes a 158.5 square meter, five-bedroom family apartment in Kóngsbakki, Breiðholt, Reykjavík, listed for 86.8 million ISK. It highlights the clever utilization of space in the three children's rooms, featuring high beds with play areas and compact desks, and notes the decorative green walls in the nursery.

items.title: Magnús og Júlíana keyptu 300 milljóna Vesturbæjarslot
items.summary: A 320 sqm house in Vesturbær, Reykjavík, built in 1945, has been sold for 300 million ISK. The buyers are Magnús Berg Magnússon and Júlíana Sól Sigurbjörnsdóttir, owners of the furniture store Officina, and Júlíana is the daughter of architect Ingibjörg Pálmadóttir. The article highlights the house's tasteful interior design, including green marble countertops and oak flooring.

items.title: Forsetaframbjóðandi selur eitt fegursta hús Reykjavíkur
items.summary: Former presidential candidate Hrannar Pétursson is selling his 182 sqm house in Reykjavík, built in 1919. The article highlights the house's historical significance and beautiful interior, including a green wooden kitchen with white marble countertops and a large Smeg stove. It is described as one of Reykjavík's most beautiful and well-maintained properties.

items.title: Ragnar Sigurðsson selur einbýli í Garðabæ
items.summary: Former football player Ragnar Sigurðsson is selling his renovated 208 sqm detached house in Garðabær. The 1969 property features a newly updated kitchen with wood fronts and stone countertops, a similarly styled bathroom, and a sauna on a large plot.

items.title: Eygló og Birgir Bieltvedt seldu raðhúsið í Fossvogi á háu verði
items.summary: The article reports on the sale of a unique 306 sqm townhouse in Fossvogur, owned by investors Birgir Þór Bieltvedt and Eygló Björk Kjartansdóttir, for 250 million ISK. The property, built in 1972 and extensively renovated, was sold to a company owned by Eygló, fetching a high price compared to average market values in the area.
items.spin_note: The headline implies an external market sale, but the body reveals the property was sold to a company owned by one of the sellers.

items.title: Nennir alls ekki að eyða sumarfríinu í að bera á pallinn
items.summary: A landscape architect offers advice on building low-maintenance decks, responding to a reader's desire to avoid upkeep during summer. The article details various durable materials like hardwood, heat-treated wood, bamboo, and composites, explaining their benefits and aesthetic properties. This guidance helps homeowners choose materials that require minimal effort while maintaining an attractive outdoor space.

items.title: Æðisleg þakíbúð á einum hæsta punkti Kópavogs
items.summary: This article describes a luxurious 291 sqm penthouse apartment in Kópavogur, designed by interior architect Pétur Hafsteinn Birgisson. Located on one of the town's highest points, it boasts unique views, five bedrooms, multiple living spaces, and a recently renovated kitchen and balconies. Features include custom-built elements and a hot tub on a covered balcony.

items.title: Sex djarfir sumarbústaðir
items.summary: This article showcases six uniquely designed summer cottages currently available for purchase in Iceland. It highlights their distinctive exterior and interior color schemes, locations, sizes, and asking prices, encouraging readers to consider buying a summer home.

items.title: Smekkfólk selur 88 milljóna sérhæð
items.summary: A four-room apartment on Hringbraut in downtown Reykjavík is for sale for 88 million ISK. The current owners, a stylist/set designer and an artist, have decorated the property with unique furniture and art, giving it a distinctive style. The apartment features three bedrooms, a bright living room, an open-plan kitchen, and a recently renovated bathroom.

items.title: Manstu þegar Logi og Svanhildur brutust inn?
items.summary: The article celebrates Smartland's 15th anniversary by recalling a past prank involving well-known Icelandic personalities. It details how Logi Bergmann Eiðsson and Svanhildur Hólm Valsdóttir rearranged all the furniture in Illugi Gunnarsson's home as a joke. The homeowner was initially alarmed, believing they had been robbed, before realizing it was a prank.
items.spin_note: The headline implies a serious crime ('broke in'), but the article describes a harmless prank where furniture was rearranged.

items.title: 225 milljóna raðhús í Garðabæ vekur athygli
items.summary: This article features a 227 sqm townhouse in Garðabær, built in 2018 and designed by architect Sigurður Hallgrímsson, currently on the market for 225 million ISK. It details the home's modern interior, including an HTH kitchen with an Italian stone countertop, an open-plan living space, and a well-appointed garden with a hot tub. The property also includes an integrated garage and a spacious driveway.

items.title: Hildur selur einstakt einbýli í Garðabæ
items.summary: Hildur Birkisdóttir, a tailor and businesswoman, has put her uniquely designed 207 sqm house in Garðabær up for sale. The article details the house's distinctive style, featuring smart kitchen fittings, marble countertops, and handcrafted elements, all reflecting Hildur's personal touch and renovation efforts. She is known for doing all the design and construction work herself.

items.title: Sigurbjartur og Kolfinna selja 90 milljóna blokkaríbúð
items.summary: Director Kolfinna Nikulásdóttir and actor Sigurbjartur Sturla Atlason are selling their 84-square-meter apartment on Mýrargata for 84.9 million ISK. The couple is upsizing, and the apartment is described as cozy and well-utilized, featuring an open kitchen and three bedrooms.
items.spin_note: The headline states a 90 million ISK price, but the article body specifies the asking price as 84.9 million ISK.

items.title: Heil­brigðis­ráð­herra slær eigið heims­met
items.summary: The article discusses the persistent and worsening issue of long waiting lists for ADHD diagnoses in Iceland. The ADHD Association has repeatedly engaged with the Minister of Health regarding this critical public health policy problem, but the situation continues to deteriorate.

items.title: Vara við net­svikum í nafni „net­glæpalög­reglunnar“
items.summary: The police in South Iceland are issuing a warning about online fraud. They advise the public to be cautious of emails impersonating "cybercrime police" and to never click on payment-related links from unknown sources.

items.title: Hópuppsögn í borginni: Störfum fækkar um 40 prósent
items.summary: The new Reykjavík City majority has initiated a mass layoff, reducing staff in the Mayor's and City Secretary's offices by 40 percent. This involves eliminating 18 jobs and relocating 9 others, with an expected annual saving of 300 million ISK for the city.

items.title: Hand­tekinn af sérsveitarmönnum undir Esjunni
items.summary: Special forces and police arrested at least one individual on Vesturlandsveg near Esja in Reykjavík. The arrest occurred around 5 PM today.

items.title: „Mann­réttindi ekkert fitu­lag“
items.summary: Minority representatives in the Reykjavík City Council are criticizing newly announced budget cuts within the city system. They express regret over the closure of the human rights office and argue that the efficiency measures were rushed through.

items.title: Kastaðist af hjólinu þegar ekið var á hann
items.summary: A cyclist was hit by a vehicle in Iceland, causing them to be thrown off their bike and land on a sidewalk curb. The injured cyclist was transported to the emergency room, but the extent of their injuries is currently unknown.

items.title: Borgarstarfsmenn taka pokann sinn og kapp­hlaup við tímann í Venesúela
items.summary: The Mayor of Reykjavík announced extensive organizational changes within the city administration, projected to save 300 million ISK annually. These changes include the layoff of eighteen city employees, the relocation of nine others, and the abolition of the human rights office and council.
items.spin_note: The headline includes a second, unrelated clause about a 'race against time in Venezuela' that is not present in the article body.

items.title: Mikill vöxtur í tækni- og hugverkaiðnaði
items.summary: The Icelandic technology and intellectual property industry experienced significant growth in spring, with revenues increasing by 12% year-over-year to nearly 120 billion ISK. This growth was particularly strong in IT, especially data center operations, where turnover almost tripled. The report from Statistics Iceland also noted growth in fishing and aquaculture, while tourism saw a decline.

items.title: Tveir neituðu sök en ekki næst í þann þriðja í Höfðatorgsmáli
items.summary: Two of the three defendants in the Höfðatorg attempted murder case pleaded not guilty at their arraignment in Reykjavík. The third defendant, accused of beating the victim, could not be reached as he is currently in Jordan. The men are accused of driving into, beating, and stabbing the victim, who sustained life-threatening injuries, and the victim is seeking 10 million ISK in damages.

items.title: Fylgir starfi lögreglu að umgangast fólk með smitsjúkdóma
items.summary: A police officer is suspected of contracting tuberculosis in a holding cell from an infected detainee. The head of the police union states that officers frequently encounter infectious diseases and there is insufficient awareness and protection regarding infection prevention in their work. The incident highlights concerns about safety protocols for police officers in detention environments.

items.title: Borgin varar við svikaskilaboðum um ógreidd bílastæðagjöld
items.summary: The City of Reykjavík has issued a public warning about fraudulent SMS messages claiming to be from the city's parking fund regarding unpaid fees. The city clarifies that it does not send such messages and advises citizens not to respond or click on any links in these scam attempts.

items.title: Til skoðunar að bæta við neyðarnúmeri
items.summary: Approximately 6,000 older mobile phones in Iceland are currently unable to connect to the 112 emergency number following the shutdown of 2G and 3G networks. The Telecommunications Agency is considering activating a temporary 7-digit emergency number to address this issue. However, this alternative number would not provide the same location tracking capabilities as 112.

items.title: Hefja brottvísanir fanga fyrir mánaðamót
items.summary: Iceland is beginning to deport foreign prisoners who have served one-third of their sentence, under a new temporary law. Nine prisoners are expected to be deported in the next two weeks, with the first before month-end. This policy primarily targets drug couriers with no ties to Iceland, aiming to streamline the justice system.

items.title: Nýju deiliskipulagi fyrir Suðurlandsbraut hafnað
items.summary: Reykjavík's environment and planning council, under its new majority, rejected a proposed zoning plan for Suðurlandsbraut. This plan was part of the Borgarlína public transport project and included dedicated lanes and pedestrian paths. The rejection was due to concerns about its impact on local businesses and parking, with the council stating the plan's transport assumptions need revision.

items.title: Öllum upplýsingafulltrúum borgarinnar sagt upp
items.summary: Reykjavík City's Office of Communications and Events has been shut down, resulting in the layoff of all information officers and most other staff. The city council approved this decision, affecting 10 out of 14 employees, who were immediately dismissed without working their notice periods.

items.title: Háskólinn á Bifröst í viðræðum við Byggðastofnun um lánveitingu
items.summary: The University of Bifröst is in discussions with the state development agency Byggðastofnun regarding a potential loan to renovate its properties in Norðurárdalur. The university has unsuccessfully tried to sell these properties for two years and now aims to put them to better use, possibly through leasing. The institution, largely state-funded, has a history of significant debt write-offs by another state agency related to these properties.
items.spin_note: The title implies a more advanced stage of loan discussions than the body, which states no application has been finalized and news is premature.

items.title: Mannréttindaskrifstofa lögð niður og uppsagnir á skrifstofu borgarstjóra
items.summary: Reykjavík City has shut down its Human Rights Office and the Office of Communications and Events, leading to layoffs and reassignments within the Mayor's office. This restructuring is part of the new city council majority's 100-day plan to streamline operations and reduce costs, with the Mayor citing annual savings of hundreds of millions.

items.title: Þunn þjóðhátíðarútgáfa/Bolur Íslands, sverð þess og skjöldur
items.summary: This article reviews Hipsumhap's new album, "Algrím hjartans," which was released on Icelandic National Day. The reviewer praises the artist's more personal lyrics but ultimately criticizes the album for feeling rushed and lacking a cohesive vision. The album received a rating of two and a half stars, indicating a mediocre reception.

items.title: Útboð hafið fyrir framkvæmdir við fangelsið að Stóra-Hrauni
items.summary: The State Properties agency has opened a tender for earthwork related to the construction of a new high-security prison at Stóra-Hraun. This new facility will accommodate 128 inmates and is intended to replace the existing Litla-Hraun prison. The current tender covers site preparation, road construction, utility installation, and other foundational work for the first phase of the project.

items.title: Björgunarsveitir aðstoða kalt og hrakið göngufólk á Suðurlandi
items.summary: Rescue teams in South Iceland responded to three separate calls for assistance due to cold and wet weather conditions. Hikers and tourists required help, with one showing signs of hypothermia and others getting their vehicle stuck. Rescue efforts were successful in reaching and assisting those in distress.

items.title: Umfangsmiklar uppsagnir í Ráðhúsi Reykjavíkur – Fækka starfsfólki um 40%
items.summary: Reykjavík City Hall is undergoing extensive layoffs, with a 40% reduction in staff. This represents a significant policy decision by the municipal government, impacting city administration, services, and the local economy.

items.title: Fyrst Evrópuþjóða til að slökkva alveg á 2G og 3G
items.summary: Iceland is the first European country to fully shut down its 2G and 3G mobile networks. This transition has created a problem where some phones, particularly those used by tourists, may be unable to dial the 112 emergency number. Efforts are underway to inform visitors, but many tourism operators are not actively participating.

items.title: Geta ekki slegið föstu hvort drónar hafi flogið yfir Kaupmannahöfn
items.summary: Danish police have been unable to confirm whether drones flew over Copenhagen airport in September, despite a four-hour air traffic shutdown as a precaution. An investigation into the incident, which was initially described by the Prime Minister as the most serious attack on critical infrastructure in Denmark's history, concluded without definitive proof of drones. Police spokesmen stated they could neither prove nor disprove the presence of drones, though something unexplained was observed.

items.title: Ernu Athichu enn leitað
items.summary: Police in the capital region are searching for 17-year-old Erna Athichu Jónsdóttir, who has been missing since Monday. The article provides a description of Erna and asks anyone with information to contact the police.

items.title: Gagnrýnendur ekki sannfærðir um brottvísunarstöð eftir fund
items.summary: The Social Democratic Alliance held a meeting to address internal party dissatisfaction regarding new legislation for a deportation center. While an MP claimed attendees were more satisfied after the discussion, critics stated that while the discussion was good, they remained unconvinced about the policy itself. The article highlights ongoing debate within the party and the need for follow-up on the law's implementation and alternative solutions.

items.title: Sanna óskaði eftir „smá andrými“ til að lesa gögn um uppsagnir
items.summary: Reykjavík City Council approved the mayor's proposal for organizational changes, leading to the termination of all city information officers. City councilor Sanna Magdalena Mörtudóttir expressed concerns about the short notice given for the decision and questioned its overall benefit for the city and its residents.

items.title: Í súld og sumaryl ég samdi þetta lag
items.summary: This article provides a roundup of recent music releases from various Icelandic artists and bands, including Quarashi, Moses Hightower, and Ólafur Arnalds. It also highlights Quarashi's upcoming concert in Laugardalshöll and Moses Hightower's forthcoming album.

items.title: Fjárhagsstaða hefur meiri áhrif á líðan en áður
items.summary: A new report from the Directorate of Health reveals that mental health, sleep, stress, and happiness in Iceland have stagnated or worsened over the past decade. The report highlights a significant correlation between financial status and well-being, with those struggling financially experiencing much poorer outcomes. Experts are calling for government action to address increasing inequality and its effects on health, particularly concerning housing security and economic mobility for younger generations.

items.title: Óttast að fleiri uppsagnir séu í uppsiglingu
items.summary: The article reports on significant organizational changes within Reykjavík city hall, leading to 27 out of 42 positions being affected in the mayor's and city secretary's offices. The Social Democratic Alliance expresses concern over these cuts, particularly the planned abolition of the city's Human Rights Office and Council.

items.title: Tillaga borgarstjóra: Leggur niður teymi, ráð og tvær skrifstofur
items.summary: The mayor of Reykjavik has proposed and had approved a major restructuring of the city administration. This involves dissolving two offices and two councils, eliminating 18 jobs, and reassigning responsibilities for human rights, communications, and policy development. The changes aim to increase efficiency and reduce costs by an estimated 80-120 million ISK annually for each major area.

items.title: Lögregla naut aðstoðar sérsveitar undir Esjunni
items.summary: The Metropolitan Police utilized special forces in an operation near Esja. The brief report confirms the involvement of special police units, with images showing multiple police vehicles surrounding another car at the scene.

items.title: Vilja byggja upp nýtt og minna samskiptateymi í borginni
items.summary: The Mayor of Reykjavík, Hildur Björnsdóttir, announced extensive layoffs and restructuring within her office and the city secretary's office, affecting 27 out of 42 positions. This move aims to reduce the city's operating costs by 280-330 million ISK annually, primarily through salary savings. The city plans to establish a smaller communications team focused on marketing and image, while human rights and equality tasks will be moved closer to service users rather than being outsourced.
items.spin_note: The headline emphasizes building a new team, but the article's core content is about extensive layoffs and restructuring within the city administration to achieve cost savings.

items.title: Laxey lauk 6,7 milljarða króna hlutafjárútboði
items.summary: Laxey, an Icelandic land-based aquaculture company, successfully completed a 6.7 billion ISK share offering, exceeding its initial target. The capital will fund the third phase of its development in Vestmannaeyjar, including a new smolt station and expansion towards a 35,000-ton annual salmon production capacity. This significant investment highlights the company's growth and its role as a major employer in the region.

items.title: Viljayfirlýsing um uppbyggingu baðlóns og hótels
items.summary: The Grundarfjörður town council has approved a letter of intent with JAE ehf. for the potential development of tourism infrastructure. This agreement focuses on the research and feasibility studies for building a bath lagoon and a luxury hotel in the area, with initial findings expected by October 1st.

items.title: Biður fólk að panta ekki gáma hjá AB gámum
items.summary: A Selfoss-based carpenter, Atli Bjarnason, is warning the public about a scam where fraudsters are using his former company's name, AB gámar, to sell non-existent containers. Victims are being tricked into transferring money to personal accounts, not the company's. Bjarnason has reported the fraud to the police, but no detective has been assigned to the case yet.

items.title: Rýmri heimildir fyrir rafsendibíla
items.summary: The Minister of Infrastructure has signed a regulation change allowing drivers with a standard B-class license (held for 2+ years) to operate heavier electric and alternative fuel delivery vans, up to 4,250 kg. This policy aims to support the energy transition and equalize the status of eco-friendly vehicles in freight transport, reducing the need for commercial driving licenses for these vehicles. The industry welcomes the change but urges further alignment with broader EU regulations.

items.title: Atvinnuleysi 5,6% í maí
items.summary: The article reports that the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in Iceland was 5.6% in May, with 13,100 people aged 16-74 unemployed. This represents little change from the previous month, though employment and labor force participation saw slight increases. Unemployment was notably higher among young people (16-24 years old) at 23.8%, likely due to summer job seeking.

items.title: Jóhanna nýr framkvæmdarstjóri PROPR
items.summary: Jóhanna Jóhannesdóttir has been appointed CEO of PROPR, a new Icelandic company specializing in marketing for real estate development. PROPR aims to help construction and real estate development firms increase visibility and reduce risk for their projects, having already worked on notable developments like Orkureitur and Háaleiti.

items.title: Samþykktu rýmri fjárfestingarheimildir lífeyrissjóða
items.summary: Parliament has approved new legislation that grants Icelandic pension funds broader investment powers. These changes, effective July 1st, aim to allow funds more flexibility in managing assets, including investments in unlisted properties, to better secure future pension payments for members. The goal is to remove obstacles and improve return opportunities for the funds.

items.title: Krónan tekin inn í TIPS-kerfi Seðlabanka Evrópu
items.summary: The Central Bank of Iceland and the European Central Bank have signed an agreement for the Icelandic króna to join the TIPS real-time payment settlement system. From 2028, this integration will allow real-time payments in króna to be settled within the European system, enhancing payment processing security and efficiency in Iceland and aligning with international standards.

items.title: „Áhyggjuefni“ hvað verður fyrir niðurskurðarhnífnum
items.summary: Reykjavík City Council approved significant administrative changes, including the abolition of two offices and 18 jobs. Minority parties expressed concern that these cuts target crucial areas like human rights, equality, public health, and the Green Plan, fearing a reduction in political and professional oversight. The majority defended the changes as a move towards efficiency and value for residents.

items.title: Síldarvinnslan stækkar skrifstofuhús sitt í Neskaupstað
items.summary: Síldarvinnslan is expanding its office building in Neskaupstaður by adding a new floor and a separate lift and technical room. The new 385-square-meter floor will be constructed using cross-laminated timber (CLT) units, a material increasingly used in Iceland for its lightweight, fast installation, and environmental benefits. The project, involving multiple contractors, began in May and is expected to be completed next spring, providing modern office space.

items.title: Mannréttindaskrifstofa einnig lögð niður
items.summary: The Reykjavík City Human Rights Office has been shut down following a city council decision, leading to layoffs and reassignments. Mayor Hildur Björnsdóttir had advocated for the closure, citing the office's annual cost of hundreds of millions and Reykjavík being the only municipality to operate such an office.

items.title: Tekist á um nýtt fyrirkomulag á fyrsta fundi
items.summary: The Reykjavík city council's new preschool and daycare board held a contentious first meeting. Employee and management representatives criticized the majority's proposal to discuss abolishing the single teaching license and shortening preschool teacher education, as well as the restructuring of the education boards. The debate centers on the importance of preschool education, teacher qualifications, and the administrative framework for schools in the city.

items.title: Þrjú útköll í einu: Ofkældist á Fimmvörðuhálsi
items.summary: Rescue teams responded to three separate incidents in the Icelandic highlands. One involved a hiker suffering from hypothermia on Fimmvörðuháls, while others were wet and cold. Another call-out concerned a tourist in Kerlingarfjöll, and a third involved a couple whose car got stuck north of Sultartangarlón.

items.title: Einfalda og nútímavæða byggingarreglugerð
items.summary: The Housing and Construction Authority (HMS) has introduced proposed changes to Iceland's building regulations. The aim is to simplify the complex and outdated rules, making the construction industry more efficient and competitive without compromising quality. Key changes include reducing the length of regulatory chapters, lessening oversight for simple private structures, and implementing a digital building permit application process standardized across all municipalities.

items.title: Tilkynnt um uppsagnirnar fyrir fram
items.summary: Reykjavík City has announced layoffs and organizational changes, including the closure of the Office of Communications and Events, the Human Rights Office, and the Mayor's Office Policy and Development Team. These measures are attributed to cost-cutting and restructuring efforts, with several employees losing their jobs or being reassigned.

items.title: Umfangsmiklar breytingar: 18 störf lögð niður
items.summary: Reykjavík City is implementing extensive administrative changes, including the elimination of 18 jobs and the restructuring of several offices like human rights and communications. These measures aim to save 280-330 million ISK annually, as the city's mayor stated current operations are financially unsustainable for statutory services. The changes, approved by the city council, also involve tightening financial controls and reducing employee travel.

items.title: Ráða í sex til sjö ný störf
items.summary: Reykjavík City is undergoing administrative restructuring, which includes eliminating 18 positions and moving 9 others, primarily within the Mayor's and City Secretary's offices. Despite the layoffs, 6-7 new positions will be created as part of the changes. These measures are projected to save the city 280-330 million ISK annually in operating costs.
items.spin_note: The headline highlights new hires but omits the context of 18 positions being eliminated as part of the same restructuring.

items.title: Niðurrif í fullum gangi á hluta Flataskóla í Garðabæ
items.summary: Demolition is underway on older sections of Flataskóli school in Garðabær, a project managed by H2Orka and overseen by VSB Verkfræðistofa. Approximately 1,170 square meters of concrete school buildings, built between 1958 and 1993, are being removed. This demolition is part of a larger redevelopment and renewal plan for the school area, with completion anticipated by mid-August 2026.

items.title: Opnun Hornafjarðarfljótabrúar langþráð en há veggjöld komi á óvart
items.summary: The Hornafjarðarfljót bridge and a new road have opened, shortening the Ring Road by 12 km and improving connectivity for the local community. While the opening was long-awaited, the mayor of Hornafjörður expressed surprise and concern over the high toll fees, questioning if less populated areas are being charged more than populous ones.

items.title: Jökulfell ehf. með eina tilboðið í vetrarþjónustu á Suðausturlandi
items.summary: The Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration received only one bid for a three-year winter service contract on a key route in Southeast Iceland. The bid from Jökulfell ehf. was 233.2 million ISK, which is 25.1% higher than the estimated cost. The agency is now reviewing the offer for snow removal and anti-icing services.

items.title: Synjaði umdeildu deiluskipulagi á Suðurlandsbraut
items.summary: The new city council majority in Reykjavík has rejected a controversial zoning plan for Suðurlandsbraut, citing concerns that it would restrict local businesses and is based on outdated transportation assumptions. This decision, which delays the first phase of the Borgarlína public transport project, was met with opposition from the Social Democratic Alliance, who argue it jeopardizes crucial infrastructure improvements. The majority intends to re-evaluate the project in light of broader city interests and a revised transport strategy.

items.title: 30.06.2026 Sambyggð 14 í Þorlákshöfn: Viðhald og Endurbætur 2026
items.summary: The homeowners association of Sambyggð 14 in Þorlákshöfn is seeking bids for extensive exterior maintenance and renovations. The project includes tearing down old cladding, pouring new foundations for window systems, constructing pavements, and enlarging balconies. Bids are due by June 30, 2026, with project completion expected by April 8, 2027.

items.title: 20.08.2026 Reykjavíkurborg býður út trjáfellingar og hirðingu grænna svæða
items.summary: Reykjavík City is issuing a tender for a framework agreement covering tree felling and the maintenance of green areas throughout the city. This service, managed by the Environment and Planning Department, includes tasks such as thinning forests, timber extraction, and pruning. The agreement will initially be for one year, with options for three one-year extensions, potentially lasting up to four years.

items.title: 15.07.2026 Grundarfjarðarbær auglýsir starf skipulags- og/eða byggingarfulltrúa
items.summary: Grundarfjarðarbær is advertising for a planning and/or building official. The role involves managing planning and building permits, overseeing construction, and participating in the town's ongoing development, including new infrastructure and community projects. The municipality is seeking professionals with backgrounds in urban planning, architecture, engineering, or related fields.

items.title: 20.08.2026 Jarðvinna boðin út fyrir nýtt öryggisfangelsi á Stóra-Hrauni
items.summary: Framkvæmdasýslan – Ríkiseignir has issued a tender for extensive earthworks for a new 128-bed high-security prison at Stóra-Hraun, replacing the current facility at Litla-Hraun. This significant government project will be built in two phases, with the first phase including general prison wards, a school, workshops, and staff facilities. The tender covers site preparation, utility installation, and other foundational work for this major infrastructure development.

items.title: HMS leggur til einfaldari og nútímalegri byggingarreglugerð
items.summary: The Housing and Construction Authority (HMS) has proposed a new, simplified, and modernized building regulation. The aim is to streamline the building permit process, enhance consumer protection, and reduce construction costs by eliminating unnecessary administrative burdens and introducing risk-based supervision. This initiative is part of a broader government effort to improve efficiency and foster innovation in the Icelandic construction sector.
